fails.defect: Rationale C is factually wrong: 'Hooker was a minister, but Williams and Hutchinson were not.' Roger Williams WAS a minister — Princeton Ch 6 calls him 'a minister in the Salem Bay settlement' and Barron's Ch 4 calls him 'a devout Puritan minister who became an important dissenter in Massachusetts.' The rationale teaches a false fact. Key A stands; fix rationale C.

Difficulty over-tagged 4 -> 3: the key is a near-verbatim restatement of the passage's final sentence ('The difference was not the climate... but what the settlers came to do and how they organized themselves'). Direct-from-stimulus restatement, same class as the 2.5/2.6/2.7 over-tags.

Rationale C is factually wrong: 'The middle colonies were the tolerant ones — Pennsylvania and Rhode Island welcomed dissenters.' Rhode Island is a NEW ENGLAND colony, not a middle colony — Barron's Ch 4 lists the New England colonies as Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Connecticut, and New Hampshire, and the middle colonies as New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Delaware. The rationale contradicts the lesson itself, which places Rhode Island in the New England dissenters section. Key B stands; fix rationale C.

items.my_pick: all 3 parts answered (b/c from the lesson, not the painting)

notes: Salem appears only in the worked item (SAQ 0042), not in the narrative; the model answer's 'the colony later apologized' is taught only there. Acceptable — the worked item is part of the lesson — but the narrative never mentions the trials.
Maryland 'began in 1632' is charter shorthand: the charter was granted in 1632, Princeton's own table lists Maryland (1633), and the settlement was 1634. Defensible; the books vary among themselves.

SAQ 0044 parts (b) and (c) are not answerable from the painting alone — the cause (Berkeley's refusal) and the consequence (turn toward race-based slavery laws) come only from the lesson's worked item, and the narrative explicitly defers Bacon's Rebellion to the next lesson. Same accepted pattern as Unit 1 SAQ 0013(c)/0027(c)/0029(c): SAQ (c) legitimately requires knowledge beyond the stimulus.

method: Read the lesson end to end as a student first, blind-solved all 35 items from the blind files alone, then adjudicated against the live question files. Both lesson images viewed with my own eye (East Prospect: title cartouche confirms 'taken by GEORGE HEAP... under the Direction of NICHOLAS SCULL'; Commons file page confirms author Gerard Vandergucht after Scull's 1754 original, engraver Thomas Jefferys — 'Thomas Vandergucht' does not exist; Pyle painting matches its description: armed men with muskets marching through a burning town at night, smoke and flames, drummer at right). Maryland date and servant-mortality claims checked against the books (Princeton lists Maryland 1633; Princeton: 'indentured servants... did not survive their term of service' — the lesson's 'nearly half died' is supported). All 30 MCQ blind picks matched keys; SAQ parts 12/12; LEQ outline 6/6. Length bounds checked in code: all generals 60-76w and strictly shorter than their questions; all key explanations 15-35w (per-option rationale length, 1-2 lines); no key option sole longest by more than 1 word; zero trap-language hits across all 35 files.

notes.note: Rationale C ('Steady growth is what the historian would expect') does not address the option's overclaim ('rising every single year without fail') — the table has only three data points and cannot show year-by-year growth. Conclusion is right; reasoning is loose. Minor.

General step 3 ('By 1751 Pennsylvania was already the most diverse colony in America') states a superlative background claim without a Background tag. Same claim appears in 0220 rationale A. Add the tag or soften.

General step 2 and rationale C state the return flow (sugar, rum back to New England) without a Background tag — the passage shows only New England selling TO the islands; the return flow is lesson content, not stimulus content. Add the tag.
